about: The one list of fitness metrics the Coach can show (the athlete, Nov 12, 2026: "clean up the cards and structure first", tiles that unlock with new hardware, an Add a metric button "populated with the catalog by sport/activity category"). Each metric is listed once: its category, what it tells you, the inputs it needs, and how to unlock a missing input. Which metrics an athlete shows is their own coach/fitness_layout.json (rows fit_kpi); every key there must be listed here. coach/tools/catalog.py reads this file and the athlete's data and works out, per metric, whether its inputs are connected (ready) or not (locked); build_dashboard.py publishes the result as cat_cat, cat_input and cat_metric rows; the page file metrics.js draws locked tiles and the Add a metric list. `starts` are the sets a new coach begins with for each thing a person can train for (setup/personalize.py). Some metrics are simple figures with no level ladder (catalog.py `figures`: longest ride or run, habit counts, best lift); they have no marker and are drawn by metrics.js from the cat_metric row's value, chip and note. A metric with `fallback_for` (an input key) stands in for riders without that input: a new coach starts with it only when that input is missing, and it stays in the Add a metric list for everyone (bikespeed for bike_power, 6.55.0). To add a metric: the tool that computes its marker, then one entry here, then a proposal the athlete approves. Requests from athletes (the dashboard's "Want to track something else?") arrive in coach/metric_requests.csv and are proposals for this file, never automatic. Every metric also names its step (habit, capacity, performance: the skill tree, the athlete, Nov 12, 2026) and its ladder; the ladders list is the one home of rungs and rules (coach/tools/ladders.py reads it).

inputs.label: runs recorded with heart rate
inputs.have: a watch that records your runs with GPS and heart rate
steps: Record a run with your watch (or with Strava, if your coach reads workouts from Strava).
A few easy runs on flat ground fill the tile within days.

inputs.label: bike power
inputs.have: power in watts, from a smart trainer or a power meter
steps: Already have a smart trainer or a power meter? Pair it once with your watch or ride app so rides record watts.
Do one steady ride of 30 minutes or more.
The tile fills in the next morning.

inputs.label: a recorded swim
inputs.have: a swim recorded on your watch
steps: Start a Pool Swim on your watch and set the pool length.
Swim 400 or more without long stops.
The tile fills in the next morning.

inputs.label: a Garmin watch
inputs.have: second-by-second climbing data, which the coach can read from Garmin watches only for now
steps: This one reads the detailed track of hilly runs and hikes, which arrives from Garmin Connect.
With a Garmin watch connected, two or three hilly runs or hikes fill the tile.

inputs.label: a Garmin watch
inputs.have: the VO2max estimate, which the coach can read from Garmin watches only for now
steps: Garmin estimates VO2max from outdoor runs with GPS and heart rate, and from rides with power.
With a Garmin watch connected, the estimate arrives after a few such sessions.

inputs.label: a power meter on your bike
inputs.have: power in watts on an outdoor ride, from a power meter on the bike (pedals, crank or hub)
steps: Outdoor rides are measured by speed only until the bike itself reports watts. Nothing needs buying: your indoor tiles already cover your bike fitness.
If you do have a power meter, pair it once with your watch or bike computer.
Do one outdoor ride of 30 minutes or more. The tile fills in the next morning.

inputs.label: a swim with heart rate
inputs.have: a swim recorded with heart rate on your watch
steps: Start a Pool Swim on your watch with wrist heart rate on (or wear a swim heart rate strap).
Swim 400 or more at an easy, steady effort.
The tile fills in the next morning.

inputs.label: an outdoor ride with heart rate
inputs.have: an outdoor ride recorded with heart rate, from your watch or a chest strap
steps: Record an outdoor ride with your watch, heart rate on.
Ride some flat road at an easy, steady effort: the tile reads the flat miles near your easy heart rate.
The tile fills in the next morning.

inputs.label: a grip gauge
inputs.have: a hand grip gauge (dynamometer) to squeeze once a month
steps: Nothing needs buying: this tile is optional.
If you have a grip gauge, tell your coach in chat ("I have a grip gauge").
Your coach adds a monthly squeeze question to your Check-in tab; the tile fills in from your first answer.

inputs.label: daily step counts
inputs.have: a step count for each day from your watch, ring or phone
steps: Wear your watch or ring through the day, or carry your phone.
Let it sync as usual.
The tile fills in after a few days of counts.

inputs.label: intensity minutes
inputs.have: moderate and vigorous minutes for each day, which Garmin watches record
steps: Garmin watches record these on their own: wear the watch through the day.
Rings and Apple Watch do not send them to the coach yet; Weekly training hours shows a similar picture from your recorded sessions.

metrics.name: Run pace at easy effort
metrics.what: How fast you run at an easy, fixed heart rate. Faster at the same heart rate means a bigger aerobic engine.

metrics.name: Run time
metrics.what: Your best time over a race distance inside any run: 5K, with the mile, 10K, half and full marathon behind the Distance switch. The 5K is a repeatable test that sets your run paces.

metrics.name: Long run
metrics.what: Your longest run in the last six weeks, road or trail.

metrics.name: Running to plan
metrics.what: Weeks your running matched your plan, counted in weeks held. Volume counts as sticking to the plan, never as more is better.

metrics.name: Sustainable trail speed
metrics.what: How fast you cover any trail at easy effort, climbs and runnable ground together.

metrics.name: Climbing at easy effort
metrics.what: How much height you gain per hour on real climbs at a fixed heart rate.

metrics.name: Time on feet
metrics.what: Your longest outing on foot in the last four weeks. It decides whether a long trail day is finishable.

metrics.name: Trail durability
metrics.what: How well your efficiency holds late in a long trail run.

metrics.name: Trail outings
metrics.what: Weeks with a trail run or hike in the last two, counted in weeks held.

metrics.name: Bike power at easy effort
metrics.what: The watts you hold at an easy, fixed heart rate: your aerobic engine on the bike.

metrics.name: Bike FTP
metrics.what: The power you could hold for about an hour, with watts per kilogram. It sets your bike zones.

metrics.name: Bike time
metrics.what: Your best time over a race distance inside an outdoor ride: 40K, with 20K, 90K, 100K and 100 miles behind the Distance switch. The bike's version of the 5K time.

metrics.name: Outdoor bike power
metrics.what: Your average power on outdoor rides, not only on the trainer.

metrics.name: Bike speed at easy effort
metrics.what: How fast you ride flat road at your easy heart rate: your bike engine when there is no power meter or trainer. Wind and group riding move it, so read it over several rides.

metrics.name: Long ride
metrics.what: Your longest ride in the last six weeks.

metrics.name: Rides to plan
metrics.what: Weeks your riding matched your plan, counted in weeks held.

metrics.name: Swim pace
metrics.what: Your pace per 100 in a steady swim, with your best 100, 400, 750 and 1500 behind the Distance switch.

metrics.name: Swim pace at easy effort
metrics.what: Your swim pace scaled to one easy heart rate, the way run pace is: faster at the same heart rate means a bigger swim engine. Wrist heart rate in water often reads low, so read it over several swims.

metrics.name: Longest swim
metrics.what: Your longest swim in the last six weeks against the swim your event calls for.

metrics.name: Swim habit
metrics.what: Weeks you were inside your swim minimum, counted in weeks held.

metrics.name: Lift strength
metrics.what: Your estimated best single lift, from the sets you log on the Lifts tab.

metrics.name: Grip strength
metrics.what: Your squeeze strength, tested once a month.

metrics.name: Strength
metrics.what: Progress on your main lifts, from the sessions you log on the Lifts tab.

metrics.name: Push-up test
metrics.what: A monthly push-up test, ranked against adults your age and sex (ACSM).

metrics.name: Pull lift
metrics.what: Your routine's loaded pull: load is the level, reps are the steps.

metrics.name: Push lift
metrics.what: Your routine's loaded press: load is the level, reps are the steps.

metrics.name: Squat lift
metrics.what: Your routine's loaded squat: the level is the load, the steps are your reps climbing to the top of the range on every set.

metrics.name: Hinge lift
metrics.what: Your routine's loaded hinge (deadlift pattern): load is the level, reps are the steps.

metrics.name: Strength habit
metrics.what: Weeks you hit your strength sessions, counted in weeks held.

metrics.name: Brisk walk pace
metrics.what: Your fastest pace on a recorded walk of a mile or more in the last six weeks.

metrics.name: Walking and hiking habit
metrics.what: Weeks with a recorded walk or hike, counted in weeks held.

metrics.name: Aerobic engine (VO2max)
metrics.what: Your watch's VO2max estimate against people of your age and sex.

metrics.name: Durability
metrics.what: How little your heart rate drifts in long steady sessions: the back half of any long event.

metrics.name: Consistency
metrics.what: Weeks with three or more training days, counted in weeks held. Showing up predicts progress better than any single session.

metrics.name: Training hours to plan
metrics.what: Weeks your training time matched your plan, out of the last 12, every sport.

metrics.name: Daily steps
metrics.what: Weeks your average steps reached your target, counted in weeks held.

metrics.name: Weekly active minutes
metrics.what: Weeks with 150 or more active minutes, hard minutes counted twice, as public health guidelines count them. Counted in weeks held.

ladders.label: Habit levels (3-3-3)
ladders.rule: The 3-3-3 rule: three days, then three weeks, then three months. Three days is three sessions inside three weeks. Weeks and months count the weeks held in a row. A week counts at 80% of your plan, or your own minimum when no plan is on record. A missed week starts the count again from zero. Past three months, the months held keep counting as extra credit.

ladders.label: Readiness levels
ladders.rule: Read against your biggest registered or planned event in the next year: a road race, trail ultra, ride or triathlon leg. Two checks: your longest session in six weeks, and your usual week (four-week average). Long session: three quarters of a road run (22 mi max), half an ultra (31 max), four fifths of a ride, all of a swim. Usual week: about the race distance, at most 40 mi for a run, 150 for a ride, or six tenths of an ultra up to 50. The lower check sets the level: Building under 60%, Close from 60%, Ready when both are covered. Nothing sits above Ready (coach guide).

ladders.label: Coach guide levels
ladders.rule: No trusted published norm yet, so the rungs come from you. Your figure is read against your own baseline from four or more weeks ago. Holding is within 3%, Rising 3 to 10% better, Well up 10% or more. It moves to levels against everyone when a norm is found.

ladders.label: Levels against everyone
ladders.rule: Against people of your age and sex, from Bottom 10% to Top 0.5%, with sub-levels so progress shows sooner.

ladders.label: Load levels
ladders.rule: Double progression: each level is a load, its three steps are your reps climbing to the top of the range on every set.

ladders.label: Its own levels
ladders.rule: Keeps the ladder shown on its chart.
